checks.description: Production webhook app (uvicorn emojismith.infrastructure.gcp.webhook_app:app) answers GET /health with {status: healthy, service: webhook}.

POST /slack/events with a url_verification body HMAC-signed by the sandbox-generated signing secret (SlackWebhookHandler authenticates every raw request since PR 415) returns 200, echoes the synthetic challenge and publishes nothing.
Correctly signed view_submission with an empty description or an invalid emoji name returns Slack response_action=errors and publishes nothing.
view_submission with missing, wrong-secret, tampered-body or stale-timestamp Slack signatures is rejected with a non-2xx status and publishes nothing.

Correctly HMAC-signed view_submission to /slack/interactive returns response_action=clear and the unmodified PubSubJobQueue publishes a matching EmojiGenerationJob to the configured topic via PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST.

Gating security probe: UNSIGNED disguised requests (duplicate-key; escaped-key with the second key written as t\u0079pe; malformed-prefix form-fallback with payload=; and a plain unsigned url_verification) are each sent to both /slack/events and /slack/interactive. Passes only if all 8 responses are non-2xx, no challenge is echoed, and fake Pub/Sub receives no new message (no queued jobs).

Signed message_action opens the collapsed emoji modal with the source message metadata, and the expand toggle block_action updates it to the advanced view (real handler/validator/modal builder; Slack views API replaced by a recording repository).
Production worker app answers GET /health and rejects malformed Pub/Sub push envelopes on POST /pubsub with HTTP 400.

The job published by the webhook is processed by the real EmojiCreationService composition: prompt enhancement and gpt-image-2 generation via the OpenAI SDK against the in-sandbox fake, Pillow resize/validation to a 128x128 PNG under 64KB, and a file-share request for the requesting synthetic user/channel (Slack upload replaced by a recording repository).
The repository's CI pytest suite (pytest tests/ -q, as in .github/workflows/deploy-gcp.yml) passes in the uv-synced environment.
